title: Emphasis nested at the end of bold (`**bold *italic***`) renders with a stray asterisk
spec:
This is the Python-Markdown library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q`. When italic text closes at the same point as the bold text around it, the output is wrong. ``` markdown.markdown('This is text **bold *italic bold*** with more text') ``` Expected: ```

This is text bold italic bold with more text

``` Actual: ```

This is text bold *italic bold* with more text

``` Mid-word also fails: `**bold*italic bold***` gives `bold*italic bold*`; expected `bolditalic bold`. The underscore form `This is text __bold _italic bold___ with more text` should give the same `bold italic bold`, but it is left untouched as literal text. Mid-word underscores are not emphasis by default, so `__bold_italic bold___` must stay literal. With the `markdown.extensions.legacy_em` extension (which does allow mid-word underscores) both underscore forms should nest; currently they give `bold _italic bold_` and `bold_italic bold_`, expected `bold italic bold` and `bolditalic bold`. Existing nesting such as `**bold *italic* *italic* bold**` must keep working. The extension should also load by its dotted path, which it currently cannot.
acceptance: Both asterisk examples nest `<em>` inside `<strong>` as expected
Underscore forms behave consistently: `__bold _italic bold___` nests by default and both forms nest with `legacy_em`, while mid-word `__bold_italic bold___` stays literal by default
